display.purpose: One per page. Ink to Lavender to Mint gradient, background-clip: text. The single expressive typographic moment.

display-vivid.purpose: Enlarged hero on the six body[data-vivid] pages. Same ramp, -0.022em tracking, dark-mode violet drop-shadow bloom.

headline.purpose: Section headers, always preceded by a 3px Lavender-to-Mint accent bar that draws in with growbar on first view.

body.purpose: Running prose at 1.65 line-height. No max-width beyond the .wrap container.

label.purpose: 0.7rem, uppercase, +0.12em tracking, Ink Muted. Section kickers, HUD labels, table headers. The one place tracking opens up.

numeric.purpose: tabular-nums on live figures in widgets (.hud-score). Changing numbers must not reflow.

shadows.name: elev-1-rest
shadows.purpose: All but invisible. Used only where a single hairline reads as ambiguous.

shadows.name: elev-2-lift
shadows.purpose: The card/hero :hover state, paired with translateY(-3px) and a border shift toward Mint.

shadows.name: bloom-vivid
shadows.purpose: vivid layer only. Soft accent-tinted outer glow on .card:hover, never at rest.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: The default; matches the 0.18s-0.3s already in use.

motion.name: dur-amble
motion.purpose: Ambient loops that must never draw the eye. Minimum for any self-starting motion.

motion.name: ease-out-quint
motion.purpose: Default. Decelerates and settles, no overshoot. Nothing bounces.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Symmetric transitions where both ends matter.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action. A full pill so its silhouette marks it without extra size. No lift, no scale, no pulse on hover.
components.css: .ds-bigplay { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 44px; padding: 8px 18px; border: none; border-radius: 999px; font: 700 0.88rem/1 Inter, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.01em; color: #04211d; background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--teal, #2dd4bf), #22b8a6); box-shadow: 0 3px 10px rgba(45,212,191,0.14); cursor: pointer; transition: box-shadow 0.18s ease, filter 0.18s ease; } .ds-bigplay:hover { filter: brightness(1.04); box-shadow: 0 5px 14px rgba(45,212,191,0.2); } .ds-bigplay:active { filter: brightness(0.97); } .ds-bigplay:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--teal, #2dd4bf); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-kbd { font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 600; opacity: 0.82; }

components.name: Secondary / Toggle Button
components.description: Preset picker and in-widget toggle. Explicit 44x44 minimum. Selected state turns border and label Mint.
components.css: .ds-preset { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 44px; min-width: 44px; margin: 0 6px 6px 0; padding: 6px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border, #232d45); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--panel, #131a2b); color: var(--text, #e8ecf6); font: 400 0.85rem Inter, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease, transform 0.15s ease; } .ds-preset:hover { border-color: var(--teal, #2dd4bf); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-preset:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.985); } .ds-preset:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--teal, #2dd4bf); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-preset.ds-on { border-color: var(--teal, #2dd4bf); color: var(--teal, #2dd4bf); font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Tier Chip
components.description: The 3-green / 2-amber / 1-red depth marker. Low-alpha tint of the semantic colour; text is the contrast-locked semantic value.
components.html: Beginner Some math Real math
components.css: .ds-tier { display: inline-block; margin-bottom: 10px; padding: 2px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border, #232d45); border-radius: 999px; font: 600 0.8rem Inter, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-tier-g { color: var(--green, #4ade80); background: rgba(74,222,128,0.08); border-color: rgba(74,222,128,0.3); } .ds-tier-y { color: var(--yellow, #facc15); background: rgba(250,204,21,0.08); border-color: rgba(250,204,21,0.3); } .ds-tier-r { color: var(--red, #f87171); background: rgba(248,113,113,0.08); border-color: rgba(248,113,113,0.3); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Every raised block. Flat at rest with a 1px hairline; lifts 3px with an accent-tinted shadow on hover.
components.html:
What is a logical qubit?

Why a thousand physical qubits make one you can trust.

The calculator →
components.css: .ds-card { border: 1px solid var(--border, #232d45); border-radius: 12px; background: var(--panel, #131a2b); color: var(--text, #e8ecf6); padding: 20px 22px; transition: transform 0.18s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), border-color 0.18s ease, box-shadow 0.18s ease; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); border-color: rgba(45,212,191,0.45); box-shadow: 0 10px 28px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); } .ds-card h3 { margin: 0 0 8px; font: 700 1.05rem Inter, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-card p { margin: 0 0 12px; line-height: 1.65; } .ds-cta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 44px; color: var(--teal, #2dd4bf); text-decoration: none; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Filled with the page canvas colour (a well below the surface it sits on). Focus replaces the outline with a Mint border shift.
components.css: .ds-field { display: block; } .ds-field > span { display: block; margin-bottom: 5px; font: 400 0.86rem Inter, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; color: var(--muted, #9aa5bd); } .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border, #232d45); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--bg, #0b0f1a); color: var(--text, #e8ecf6); font: 400 0.95rem Inter, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; transition: border-color 0.18s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted, #9aa5bd); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--teal, #2dd4bf); }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Ink Muted going to Ink on hover; the active item is Ink with a 2px Mint underline. An invisible 44px hit band keeps the target honest without growing the text box.
components.html: The RaceCorrections
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 18px; align-items: center; padding: 18px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border, #232d45); } .ds-navlink { position: relative; color: var(--muted, #9aa5bd); text-decoration: none; font: 400 0.92rem Inter, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; padding-bottom: 2px; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; transition: color 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-navlink::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 50%; height: 44px; transform: translateY(-50%); } .ds-navlink:hover { color: var(--text, #e8ecf6); } .ds-navlink.ds-active { color: var(--text, #e8ecf6); border-bottom-color: var(--teal, #2dd4bf); }

components.name: Verdict Banner
components.description: The shared widget-kit result banner. Mint = good/feasible/verified, Red = bad/infeasible, Lavender = split/interpretive.
components.html:
Feasible. Every constraint is satisfied.

Split decision. It depends on what you count.
components.css: .ds-verdict { margin: 0 0 10px; padding: 11px 15px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; font: 600 1rem Inter, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-verdict-good { color: var(--teal, #2dd4bf); background: rgba(45,212,191,0.12); border-color: rgba(45,212,191,0.45); } .ds-verdict-bad { color: var(--red, #f87171); background: rgba(248,113,113,0.11); border-color: rgba(248,113,113,0.42); } .ds-verdict-split { color: var(--violet, #a78bfa); background: rgba(167,139,250,0.12); border-color: rgba(167,139,250,0.45); }

narrative.overview:
SymbiQ is a precise measuring instrument that happens to be alive. Its whole promise is that the mathematics does the judging — every game par is an optimum found by exhaustive search, every probability on screen is computed rather than chosen, every claim carries a date and a falsification condition. The visual system exists to make that trustworthy: the chrome recedes, the reading is what you look at, and the one thing that moves on its own is a faint generative lattice behind everything — the same object the site is about, actually behaving like one.

The surface is dark by default (#0b0f1a, a near-black with a blue cast) with a fully realised light theme that swaps in measured, contrast-locked values rather than naive inversions. Two accent hues carry meaning, not decoration: a lattice lavender for the quantum/theoretical half of every topic, an electric mint for the AI/operations-research/shipping half, and a signal amber reserved for "check your own systems." Depth is tonal and hairline-drawn, not shadowed. Type is a single Inter voice from the gradient-clipped hero line down to 0.7rem uppercase labels. Motion is almost entirely feedback plus one ambient layer held deliberately below the threshold of notice.

The deliberate anti-references: no springy or bouncing motion; no oversized or pulsing primary CTA; no photographic imagery anywhere; no accent used purely to look designed.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, dual-theme. Every token has a measured light-mode value; the light theme is a real design, not an inversion.
Semantic two-hue accent — lavender = quantum/theory, mint = AI/real/OR, amber = security. The colour tells you which half of the argument you are reading.
Tonal depth. A two-step surface ladder plus 1px hairlines carry hierarchy; shadow is a response to state, never a decoration.
One Inter voice from the 1.9rem hero to the 0.7rem label; hierarchy comes from weight, size and colour, not from a second family.
Motion is feedback plus one ambient layer. Nothing bounces; the only self-starting motion is a sub-threshold lattice and a slow background breath.
Layered stylesheets. style.css is the shared 24-page base; motion.css, rails.css and vivid.css are opt-in, separately cache-busted layers.

rules.name: The Colour Law
rules.body: Mint means AI / real / OR / shipping. Lavender means quantum / theory / ahead. Amber means "check your own system." Muted grey is scaffolding. A colour on this site is a claim about which half of the argument you are looking at; if a new element's colour does not answer that question, it should be muted.

rules.name: The Contrast Lock
rules.body: In light mode, ink, ink-muted, teal-accent, link, green, amber and red are the exact values a full per-node sweep proved clear 4.5:1. They are never brightened "for vibrancy" — a wrong colour still renders, passes every test, and is only caught by measuring. Enrich decorative tokens instead.

rules.name: The Two-Value Rule
rules.body: Every colour token is defined once unconditionally (that value is the dark theme) and once inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: light). A scoped override layer must redeclare the full set in its own light block, or an unconditional [data-*] selector (specificity 0,2,0) leaks its dark value past the base @media light :root (0,1,0).

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Inter carries display through label. Hierarchy is weight (400 body / 700 heading / 800 vivid hero), size, and colour — never a second family. Code samples are the only exception and use the platform monospace stack.

rules.name: The Gradient Belongs to h1
rules.body: The Ink-to-Lavender-to-Mint background-clip: text ramp is the hero line's alone. h2 gets the same ramp as a 3px bar, not as text. No other text is gradient-filled.

rules.name: Tracking Tightens With Size
rules.body: The vivid hero runs -0.022em; labels run +0.12em; body runs 0. If a new display size is added, its tracking is negative and scales with the size.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface at rest has a hairline and nothing else. If you reach for box-shadow, it is a hover, focus or drag response — state, not decoration — and it is tinted to the accent, never pure black.

rules.name: The Tonal-Ladder Rule
rules.body: Nesting depth is expressed by stepping up the surface ladder, not by stacking shadows. Canvas holds surface; surface holds a nested --bg-filled well (inputs, figure frames, .hud).

dos: Do answer the Colour Law with every new element: mint = AI/real/OR, lavender = quantum/theory, amber = check-your-system, muted = scaffolding. If the colour makes no such claim, use muted.
Do carry depth with the tonal ladder and a 1px hairline. Reach for box-shadow only as a hover/focus/drag response, and tint it to the accent.
Do give every control an explicit min-height: 44px (and min-width for icon-width buttons). A control that clears 44px by accident of its label does not clear it.
Do keep the primary action a full pill at its current size. If it needs to be more noticeable, reach for the pill silhouette or the gradient — never size, weight, lift or pulse.
Do define every new colour token in both the unconditional block and the @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) block, with the light value measured to 4.5:1 for anything that renders as text.
Do ship new motion or heavy visual layers as their own separately cache-busted stylesheet. Editing style.css is a 24-page deploy.
Do let exactly one atmospheric moment run per section — one glow, one wash. Ambient loops run at least 8s at under ~5% amplitude and must never draw the eye.
Do render diagrams as inline SVG in the HTML, inside .figscroll, so they are crawlable, survive JS-off, and stay legible at 375px.
donts: Don't add springy, bouncing or overshooting easing. Motion decelerates and settles; nothing rebounds.
Don't enlarge, animate, lift or pulse the primary CTA. Three separate rounds of feedback removed exactly those; re-adding one silently reverses a settled decision.
Don't gradient-fill any text except the h1. h2 gets the ramp as a bar.
Don't brighten a contrast-locked light-mode colour for visual punch. Enrich the glow, dot-grid and gradient-stop tokens instead, and re-measure the rendered element.
Don't introduce a second type family for hierarchy. Weight, size and colour do that job.
Don't add a second scroll-reveal mechanism — nav.js owns .reveal and is the only thing that may add that class, so a script failure leaves the page fully visible. Extend its selector instead.
Don't ship a photographic image. The generative lattice and inline SVG are the house substitutes.
Don't run git add -A in the site repo, and don't edit style.css for a change that only touches a handful of pages.
